title: SAP reportedly confirms IT security incident; Der Spiegel reports stolen employee tokens used to alter source code on GitHub
date_note: Cyber Security News (27 Nov) gives no earlier day for the detection or the theft.
geo_basis: SAP headquarters; the source names no site of the incident
summary: Cyber Security News reports that SAP confirmed an IT security incident after detecting suspicious activity. It says SAP said investigators had found no evidence so far of unauthorized access to customer business data. Der Spiegel, citing sources inside SAP, reportedly said attackers stole authentication tokens of SAP employees and used them to alter and copy source code on GitHub. SAP did not answer detailed questions.
plain: SAP is reported to have confirmed a security incident. Der Spiegel reportedly says stolen employee tokens were used to change code on GitHub; SAP says it has found no evidence so far of access to customer business data.
exec: SAP reportedly confirms an incident; no evidence so far of customer business data access, but what code was changed is not yet disclosed.
action: No action needed; for awareness. Cyber Security News says it is not yet known whether customers need to act.

validation.note: Only Cyber Security News was read; it relays SAP's statement (paraphrased) and Der Spiegel's report. India Today's report could not be loaded; SAP's own statement and the Spiegel article were not found.
